ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within circle $O$, $AB$ is a side of the inscribed regular hexagon in circle $O$, and $BC$ is a side of the inscribed regular decagon in circle $O$. What is the measure of $\angle ABC$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, connect AO, BO, CO,

$\because$ AB is a side of the inscribed hexagon in $\odot O$,

$\therefore$ $\angle AOB = \frac{360^\circ}{6} = 60^\circ$,

$AO = BO$,

$\therefore$ $\angle ABO = \frac{1}{2}(180^\circ-60^\circ) = 60^\circ$,

$\because$ BC is a side of the inscribed decagon in $\odot O$,

$\therefore$ $\angle BOC = \frac{360^\circ}{10} = 36^\circ$, BO=CO,

$\therefore$ $\angle CBO = \frac{1}{2}(180^\circ-36^\circ) = 72^\circ$,

$\therefore$ $\angle ABC = \angle ABO + \angle CBO = 60^\circ + 72^\circ = \boxed{132^\circ}$.

From the image, identify A, B, and C as points on the same circle with O as the center, and note that ray BO lies inside the drawn angle ABC, so angle ABC can be split into angle ABO plus angle OBC. method.method_draft: Use arcs and the inscribed angle theorem. From the image, read that A, B, and C lie consecutively on the upper part of the circle, with B on the minor arc from A to C; angle ABC is an inscribed angle whose intercepted arc is the arc AC not containing B.
